message.content:
This is a set put up for retail sale (GRI 3(b)), so classification turns on the component that gives the set its essential character. The set is classified under HTSUS 8206.00.00, which covers tools of two or more of headings 8202 to 8205 put up in sets for retail sale. That heading does not fit here, because the set contains items outside 8202-8205 (a level, pencil, tape measure and hardware).

The hammer is in 8205.20, the utility knife in 8211 or 8205.59, the tape measure in 9017.80, the level in 9015.80 or 9017, the pencil in 9609 and the hardware in 7317 and 7318. Since this is a mixed set, GRI 3(b) applies. The hammer is the most plausible essential-character item, as it is the principal tool and the one that gives the set its character. The alternative is the tape measure.

CBP rulings on similar mixed sets often pick the hammer. The hammer is classified under 8205.20.60: hammers and sledges with heads of metal, valued over a certain amount. The 8205.20 subheadings are 8205.20.30 (Machinists' hammers), 8205.20.60 (Other: with heads over 0.5 kg... ), and 8205.20.90, but I'm not certain of the exact split. I'll go with 8205.20.6000 as the general "other" line.
